why: offset everywhere incl. toc and CLI, validated, documented and tested
prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
`heading_offset` (0–5, default 0) is added to `markdown.Markdown` / `markdown.markdown` and as `--heading-offset N` on the command line; the full suite passes (1146 tests, 112 skipped), including 17 new ones. No linter was run (flake8 is not installed here). It is implemented as a built-in tree processor (`heading_offset`, priority 25), so it shifts hash, underline, `md_in_html` and footnote headings alike, and `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`. Docs and a changelog entry are updated. Behaviours you might not assume: - Raw HTML headings that Markdown passes through unparsed (a plain `

…

`) are not shifted; `

` is. - Only a real `int` is accepted: `True`, `1.0` and `'1'` all raise `ValueError`. - On the command line a bad or out-of-range value exits with the usual option-parser usage error rather than a `ValueError` traceback. - `parse_options` only includes `heading_offset` in its result when it is non-zero, which kept the existing CLI tests' exact-dict comparisons unchanged. - With `toc`'s `baselevel`, the offset is applied first and `baselevel` on top of it. - I also added the missing `-n, --no_lazy_ol` line to the help listing in `docs/cli.md`, since it now mirrors the real `--help` output.
